outcome: Efficacy of DFPP (reduction in anti-D/M antibody titers)
Necessity and success of intrauterine blood transfusions (IUTs)
Changes in blood parameters (albumins, globulins, complement factors, coagulation factors, white blood cells, neutrophils, hemoglobin)
cohort: The study included 6 pregnant women (5 with Rh, 1 with MN-associated maternal-fetal hemolysis) at high risk of early-onset hemolytic disease in fetus and newborn (HDFN).
finding: DFPP was found to be an effective and safe rescue therapy for pregnant women with maternal incompatible hemolytic anemia, leading to significant reductions in antibody titers and successful prolongation of pregnancy for most participants.
followup_time: The treatment duration spanned a median of 9.5 weeks (range: 1-14) during pregnancy, with follow-up until successful prolongation of pregnancy to 20 weeks for IUT or failed pregnancy.
gest_age: DFPP was initiated at a median gestational age of 14 weeks (range: 12-18), with a goal of prolonging pregnancy until at least 20 weeks of gestation for safe IUT.
